title: Data-Based Quantitative Reasoning
tagline: Year 4 — Quantitative questions set on a small table: derived columns, weighted averages, profit and share calculations

introduction.overview: Many quantitative questions arrive with a table: units and prices, hours and wages, marks and weights. The method is to add the derived columns once (revenue, profit, total cost), and then every question is a lookup or a ratio. Averages across rows must be weighted by the right quantity, and percentages must use the correct base.
introduction.placementRelevance: Table-based quantitative sets are common in placement papers because they test accuracy and organisation together.
introduction.realWorldContext: Business reports, invoices and sales summaries are tables of exactly this form.

learningObjectives: Build derived columns once and reuse them
Compute profit, margin and share from a table
Compare rows on a derived measure

prerequisiteKnowledge.quickRefresher: Revenue = units × price. Profit = units × (price − cost). Weighted average = total ÷ total weight.

coreDefinitions: Derived column: a column computed from others.
Weighted average: total of values ÷ total of weights.
Margin: profit as a percentage of revenue.
Share: part as a percentage of the whole.
Base: what a percentage is measured against.
conceptExplanation.theoreticalIntuition: A table is a set of numbers waiting to be multiplied. Do the multiplication once for every row.
conceptExplanation.visualOrMentalModel: Add revenue, cost and profit columns first. Then read each question as a lookup, a total, or a ratio of totals.

mainNarrative: Overall margin = 29,000 ÷ 151,000 = 19.2%. This is not the average of the four product margins (20%, 16.7%, 20%, 20%).
Average selling price per unit = total revenue ÷ total units = 151,000 ÷ 550 = ₹274.5.
The product with the highest profit is R (9,000), even though S has the highest margin per unit.
Always check which total (units, revenue or profit) is the base of a percentage.

deepDiveAspects.title: Per-unit versus total
deepDiveAspects.content: A high profit per unit does not give high total profit if few units are sold.

deepDiveAspects.title: Weighted vs simple averages
deepDiveAspects.content: A simple average of prices ignores how many units each price sold.

solvedExamples.title: Profit
solvedExamples.question: Product P: 120 units sold at ₹250 each, cost ₹200 each. What is the total profit?

solvedExamples.title: Weighted average
solvedExamples.question: Total revenue is ₹1,51,000 from 550 units. What is the average selling price per unit?

solvedExamples.title: Margin
solvedExamples.question: Total profit ₹29,000 on revenue ₹1,51,000. What is the overall margin?

traditionalVsShortcut.shortcutMethod: Add revenue and profit columns once; answer every question from totals and ratios of totals.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using cost as the base for margin on revenue

placementTips.eliminationTechnique: A total cannot be less than any single row.
placementTips.questionSelectionAdvice: Write derived columns beside the table.
